text: OUR OFFERINGS IS ONE SECTION AGAIN, AS THE DESIGN DRAWS IT. Three sections were doing the same job apart: a grid of six featured scheme cards, a grid of eleven persona tiles four sections later, and a What's New section after that. They are now one — three tabs (Schemes, Vacancies, Tenders), the eleven groups of the Department's mandate as chips, and beside them What's New in its own brand column. Choosing a group shows that group's own line, the portal it applies through with one action, three of its schemes with what each provides, and a link to the rest; the Senior Citizens route is a helpline, so its action reads "Call Elderline 14567" and does not open a window. THE LISTS ARE BUILT ON THE SERVER AND PASSED DOWN. The scheme master is 38 records of prose and the tender and vacancy registers are larger still; a client component importing them would put all of it in the bundle for a reader who never touches a tab. What crosses is eleven blocks and five rows for each of the other two tabs. TWO DIVERGENCES FROM THE DRAWING, both stated in the source. What's New does not move: the design draws it scrolling with a pause control, and an auto-scrolling list takes the sentence away from whoever reads slowest while a scroll region inside a card catches a phone flick and moves the list instead of the page (`data-state-completeness.md` §4). Nothing moves, so there is nothing to pause. And the tabs carry no icons: `SegmentedOption` is `{ label, value }`, and an `icon` it does not declare renders nothing while reading in the source as a feature that exists — the control wants an optional icon before this can carry them.
